spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:** The first who grieves is the inmost Divine Love from which all spiritual life proceeds. She is in sorrow because the living affections that proceed from her have been plunged into states of temptation and vastation, for they were conjoined with falsity and the persuasions of evil that corrupt the interiors. They have been held captive under the entire dominion of self-love. On what account does that Divine Love grieve, watching over them as they undergo these assaults of spiritual combat? Whenever she perceives their state and how the violence of temptation is brought upon them, she shall grieve and remain in holy sorrow on their account.

**¶3:** The second who is troubled in his inmost is the Divine Celestial Principle, whose sovereign sphere and dominion is established in the vessel of Divine Wisdom [GAP-1: — the understanding illuminated by heavenly light through which that dominion operates]. And he too is troubled in his inmost because of his five essential faculties of spiritual perception, which are set in the midst of peril from the hells. For at any time he may perceive that they are beset by assault, continually he receives the interior cry of their anguish as they call out because of the injuries and violations inflicted by the evil that attacks them in every state; and as he perceives them thus without ceasing, he grieves and mourns on account of the goods of perception that proceed from him.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The first who grieves is the first Mother of Life. She is sad because of her children who are set in affliction, for they were conjoined with the Darkness and the [poi]son. They have been bound with the entire ruling-power. For what was she grieving, [wa]tching over them taking these afflictions? Whenever she might [s]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve and be unhappy on account of them.

[The s]econd one who is troubled of heart is the First Man, whose [great]ness and kingdom is established in the li[ght] ship [of the moon]. And he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger. For any time he may see that they are given trouble, always he might hear the sound of their weeping as they cry out because of the blows and wounds of the enemy who assaults them daily; and as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[ri]eve and mourn on account of his [s]o[n]s.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading identifies the light ship as "the vessel of Divine Wisdom — the understanding illuminated by heavenly light," which in the Kephalaia's cosmological register corresponds to the Moon (the ship of living waters/reflected light), the vessel through which the First Man's celestial dominion operates via wisdom and understanding.
